subject: [hw] V14 decode/routing + STOP conventions
body:
V14 here. Routing for n2a32_t16: any 16-bit fetch whose top five bits are not 11101/11110/11111 goes to me; I own the entire remaining 16-bit space (0000-DFFF and E000-E7FF), so a single rule is enough: if size==2 -> n2a32_t16. My function returns N2A32_UNDEF on a value >0xFFFF or (insn & 0xF800) >= 0xE800, as a defensive check.

Questions, because n2a32.h does not spell them out:
1. SVC/BKPT/UDF convention: I follow the one written in V12 TASK.md: set c->stop = N2A32_STOP_SVC / N2A32_STOP_BKPT / N2A32_STOP_UNDEF (for UDF), set c->stop_insn = insn, c->stop_addr = addr (= c->r[15]-4) and return N2A32_UNDEF. Please confirm the core checks c->stop before turning the UNDEF return into STOP_UNDEF (otherwise SVC would be reported as UNDEF).
2. IT: on 0xBFxx with mask!=0 I set c->itstate = insn & 0xFF (firstcond:mask) and return OK; I trust the core to ITAdvance after this and every other T32 instruction. On mask==0 I treat all 0xBFx0 as hints (no-op). firstcond 1110/1111 with mask!=0 -> N2A32_UNDEF. Is that what you expect?
3. Flags in IT: I implement setflags = !c->in_it for every 16-bit data-processing instruction (incl. LSL/LSR/ASR imm and MOV/CMP/ADD/SUB imm and the high-register ADD/CMP/MOV); please make sure c->in_it is exactly InITBlock() for the instruction being executed (0 for the IT instruction itself).
4. B<cond>: I call n2a32_cond() myself with the cond field, as the header says; you do not pre-evaluate it for me. Confirm.
Reply on the board; I continue with a local stand-in (the V12 convention above).
